# Egret

> Egret is a 2D and 3D game engine for the browser. A whole small 2D game is one call, `play({ width, height, setup, update })`, and one file, `egret2d.js`. This page is everything needed to write one. It needs no image, sound or font file and no build step.

## The page

```html
<!doctype html>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>Game</title>
<script src="egret2d.js"></script>
<script type="module">
const { play } = Egret;

await play({
  width: 480, height: 270, background: 0x101828,
  setup(game) { /* make the sprites; called again by game.restart() */ },
  update(dt, game) { /* one step; dt is the seconds since the last one */ },
});
</script>
```

`play` makes the canvas, fills the window with it and keeps the stage's shape. Do not add a canvas, CSS or a loop. The page opens from a folder or from a server. `egret2d.js` is beside the page: it is in a release, or `node tools/pack-single-file.mjs` makes it in a checkout. In a project with modules, `import { play } from '@egret/engine/play'` is the same function.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `x`, `y` of `game.rect` and `game.circle` is the **middle** of the shape. `y` of `game.text` is the **top** of the words.
- A colour is a number, `0xRRGGBB`. A string such as `'#ff0000'` is refused.
- `dt` is in **seconds**: move by `speed * dt`, with speed in units a second.
- Give every variable of the game its value in `setup`, not where it is declared: `game.restart()` runs `setup` again.
- Declare every variable and constant the game uses above `await play(...)`: `setup` runs before that line ends, and a `const` written below it is not there yet.
- Use `game.after`, `game.every`, `game.wait` and `game.tween`, never `setTimeout`, `setInterval` or `requestAnimationFrame`.
- When a sprite leaves the game, call `game.remove(sprite)` and take it out of your own lists. It may still be set until that update ends; after that setting it throws, and its `isDisposed` is true.
- To change how a sprite looks, draw it again: `sprite.graphics.clear().beginFill(color).drawRect(-10, -10, 20, 20).endFill()`.
- A browser plays no sound before the first key or click. That is expected; do not work around it.
- An error's message says what was wrong and ends with `Cause: …`. Read it to the end before changing anything.

## Options of `play`

`width` and `height` are the stage in the game's own units, whole numbers above 0, and are required. `background` is the colour behind everything, black unless given. `setup(game)` builds the game and may be `async`; `update(dt, game)` is one step, and is not called before `setup` has finished. `parent` is an element to put the canvas in instead of filling the window. `seed` makes `game.random` repeat. `onError(error)` is told of what stopped the game, which is otherwise thrown to the console.

## Drawing

| Call | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `game.rect(x, y, width, height, color, layer?)` | A filled rectangle, its middle at (x, y) |
| `game.circle(x, y, radius, color, layer?)` | A filled circle, its middle at (x, y) |
| `game.sprite(g => …, layer?)` | A sprite with what the function draws around its own (0, 0) |
| `game.text(words, { x, y, size, color, align, bold, baseline, layer })` | Text: `size` 24, `color` white, `align` `'left'`, `'center'` or `'right'`, `baseline` `'top'` or `'middle'` |
| `game.button(words, { x, y, width, height, color, textColor, size, layer }, onTap)` | A button, its middle at (x, y); `button.label.text` changes its words |
| `await game.image('hero.png', { x, y, width, height, smooth, layer })` | A picture from a file beside the page, its middle at (x, y); one of `width`, `height` keeps its shape. Smooth, and kept clean when drawn small; `smooth: false` for pixel art |
| `game.remove(sprite)` | Takes it and what is in it off the stage |
| `game.toFront(sprite)` | Puts it in front of the others of its layer |

`g` draws with `beginFill(color, alpha?)`, `drawRect(x, y, w, h)`, `drawRoundRect(x, y, w, h, corner)`, `drawCircle(x, y, r)`, `drawEllipse(x, y, w, h)` (x, y is the top left of its box), `lineStyle(thickness, color, alpha?)`, `moveTo(x, y)`, `lineTo(x, y)`, `curveTo(cx, cy, x, y)`, `endFill()` and `clear()`; each returns `g`. A triangle is `g.beginFill(c).moveTo(0, -10).lineTo(8, 8).lineTo(-8, 8).endFill()`.

Every one of these is a sprite. Set `x`, `y`, `rotation` (degrees, clockwise), `scaleX`, `scaleY`, `alpha` (0 to 1) and `visible`; read `width` and `height`; add properties of your own (`enemy.hp = 3`). It turns and scales about its origin. Sprites are drawn in the order they were made, later ones in front.

Layers: `game.world` holds what is made, and scrolls with `game.view.x` and `game.view.y`. `game.ui` is over it and stays put; text and buttons go there. Pass `game.ui` as `layer` for a bar or a panel. Pass a sprite as `layer` to make something inside it, moving, turning and fading with it. `game.text` takes `layer: 'world'` for words that scroll with the world, and `layer: sprite` for words on a sprite.

Text: `label.text = 'Score ' + n` changes it, and `label.color` and `label.size` change those. `\n` starts a new line. It is a sprite, so it can be tweened and removed.

`game.width` and `game.height` are the stage; `game.time` is the seconds of play.

## Input

| Ask | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `game.keys.down('left', 'a')` | Whether any of these keys is held |
| `game.keys.pressed('space')` | Whether it went down since the last update |
| `game.keys.released('space')` | Whether it came up since the last update |
| `game.keys.axis()` | Arrows and WASD, a gamepad's d-pad or left stick, or a stick on the glass, as `{ x, y }`, each -1 to 1, y down |
| `game.keys.look()` | A gamepad's right stick, for looking or aiming; 0 and 0 without one |
| `game.keys.down('space', 'pad:a')` | A gamepad's buttons are keys named `pad:a`, `pad:b`, `pad:x`, `pad:y`, `pad:l1`, `pad:r1`, `pad:l2`, `pad:r2`, `pad:select`, `pad:start` and `pad:up` … `pad:right` |
| `game.touchStick()` | A stick on the glass, bottom left unless `{ x, y, radius }`; it counts in `keys.axis()`. It and the buttons below appear once a finger touches the stage, or at once with `always: true`; a mouse does not use them. Make them in `setup`: a restart takes them away |
| `game.touchButton('A', { x, y, key: 'space' })` | A round button on the glass that holds that key while a finger is on it |
| `game.pointer.x`, `game.pointer.y` | Where the mouse or finger is, on the stage; it follows the mouse with no button held |
| `game.pointer.down`, `.pressed`, `.released` | Whether it is down, went down, or came up. A press on a button or on a sprite with `onTap` is theirs and is not `pressed` |
| `game.pointer.swipe` | `'left'`, `'right'`, `'up'` or `'down'` in the update after a swipe, else `undefined` |
| `game.pointer.over(sprite)` | Whether the pointer is over the sprite |
| `game.pointer.dx`, `.dy`, `.wheel` | How far the mouse moved and the wheel turned since the last update: for looking about |
| `game.pointer.lock()`, `game.pointer.unlock()`, `game.pointer.locked` | Hides the cursor and keeps the mouse to the game, for a first-person view. Call `lock` after a click; Escape gives the mouse back |
| `game.onTap(sprite, () => …)` | Calls the function when the sprite is tapped or clicked; the one in front gets it |

A key is `'left'`, `'right'`, `'up'`, `'down'`, `'space'`, `'enter'`, `'escape'`, `'shift'`, a letter or a digit. Make every game playable with the pointer as well as keys, so it works on a phone.

## Sound

`game.sfx.play(name)` plays an effect made in code: `jump`, `coin`, `hit`, `hurt`, `explosion`, `shoot`, `powerup`, `bounce`, `pop`, `click`, `hum`, `wind`, `win`, `lose`. `game.sfx.play('coin', { volume: 0.5, pitch: 1.2 })` changes one play; `pitch` multiplies the pitch. Any other name is refused unless defined: `game.sfx.define('zap', { wave: 'saw', from: 1200, to: 200, seconds: 0.15 })`, with `wave` one of `'sine'`, `'square'`, `'saw'`, `'triangle'`, `'noise'`; a list of tones is a jingle: `game.sfx.define('chime', [{ wave: 'sine', from: 880, seconds: 0.08 }, { wave: 'sine', from: 1320, seconds: 0.3, volume: 0.4 }])`. A tone is `{ wave, from, to, seconds, volume, decay, noise }`; only `from` and `seconds` are needed. `game.sfx.loop(name, { volume, pitch, pan })` plays one again and again until `.stop()`: music made with `define`, the `hum` of an engine whose `.pitch` a game raises with its speed, the `wind`. Its `volume`, `pitch` and `pan` can be set while it plays; a pause holds it and `restart` stops it. `game.sfx.names` lists them; `game.sfx.volume` and `game.sfx.muted` act on all.

## Music

`game.music.play('battle')` writes music in code in a mood, `'calm'`, `'mystery'`, `'tense'`, `'battle'` or `'triumph'`, and loops it; one object chooses more: `game.music.play({ mood: 'battle', tempo: 150, seed: 2 })`. A new piece fades the old one out. `game.music.intensity` (0 to 1, 0.5 unless set) brings in its parts: held chords always, then a bass, drums and a tune; set it as the moment grows, and it follows over a second or so. `game.music.volume` (0.6) and `game.music.stop(seconds)`. Like sound, it is heard after the first key or click; a pause holds it and a restart stops it.

## Overlap

| Ask | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `game.overlaps(a, b)` | Whether two sprites overlap, as upright boxes |
| `game.hits(a, list)` | The first sprite of the list that overlaps `a`, or `undefined` |
| `game.hitsAll(a, list)` | Every sprite of the list that overlaps `a` |
| `game.near(a, b, distance)` | Whether their middles are within `distance`: the test for circles |
| `game.pushOut(a, b)` | How far to move `a` out of `b` by the shorter way, `{ x, y }`, or `undefined` when apart |

A sprite with `visible = false` or removed overlaps nothing; one with `alpha` 0 still does. A sprite never hits itself.

## Time and motion

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `game.after(seconds, fn)` | Calls `fn` once; returns a function that calls it off |
| `game.every(seconds, fn)` | Calls `fn` again and again; returns a function that ends it |
| `await game.wait(seconds)` | Waits, in an `async` function |
| `game.tween(sprite).to({ x: 100, alpha: 0 }, 0.3, 'quadOut')` | Moves numbers over time; starts by itself. Chain `.to`, `.wait(s)`, `.call(fn)`, `.loop(times)`: steps run one after another. Two tweens of one property fight; `game.remove` a sprite to end its tweens |
| `await game.tween(sprite).to({ y: 200 }, 0.2).done` | Waits for it to finish |
| `game.timeScale = 0.5` | Slow motion |
| `game.pause()`, `game.resume()`, `game.paused` | Stops and starts updates, timers and tweens; `update` is not called while paused, so keys are not asked, but a button still works |
| `game.restart()` | Clears the world, the ui, timers and tweens, and runs `setup` again |

Easings: `linear`, `quadIn`, `quadOut`, `quadInOut`, `cubicOut`, `backOut`, `elasticOut`, `bounceOut`.

## Feel

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `game.shake(amount = 6, seconds = 0.25)` | Shakes the world; the ui stays put |
| `game.flash(color = 0xffffff, seconds = 0.15)` | A colour over the stage that fades |
| `game.hitStop(seconds = 0.06)` | Freezes play for a moment |
| `game.burst(x, y, { color, count, speed, life, size, gravity })` | Throws pieces out from a point of the world |

Use them: a hit wants a sound, a burst and a small shake; a death wants a flash.

## Words, menus and bars

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `game.bar({ x, y, width, height, value, max, color, back, layer })` | A bar of health, time or power, on the ui unless `layer`; `x`, `y` is its top left. Set `bar.value` and it slides there; a fall leaves a pale trail |
| `game.toast('Saved')` | A short notice at the top that fades after 2 seconds, or `{ seconds }`; several stack |
| `await game.say('words', { who, choices, color, speed })` | A box of words at the bottom, shown letter by letter and wrapped; words longer than a box holds (about three lines) go on in a second box. It does not pause the game: check `game.asking`. Space, Enter, Z or a tap shows the rest, another closes it. With `choices` it gives the index chosen with the arrows and Enter or a tap; without, undefined |
| `await game.menu(['Start', 'Quit'], { title })` | A list in the middle of the stage; gives the index chosen |
| `game.asking` | Whether a box of words or a menu is open; an `update` can return early while it is |

`setup` may await them: frames are drawn while it waits, so a title menu or a first line of a story is `await game.menu(...)` in `setup`. They answer while the game is paused. Boxes asked for while one is open wait their turn. A restart takes them away.

## Chance and saves

`game.random.int(1, 6)`, `.range(0, 1)`, `.chance(0.25)`, `.pick(list)` and `.shuffle(list)`, which gives a new list. `game.save('best', score)` keeps a value between visits and `game.load('best', 0)` reads it, or gives the second argument.

## Three whole games

Each is the whole script of the page above.

### Breakout: an arcade game with a ball, lives, a win and a loss

```js
const { play } = Egret;

const W = 480,
  H = 320;
let paddle, ball, bricks, score, lives, label, vx, vy, over;

await play({
  width: W,
  height: H,
  background: 0x101828,
  setup(game) {
    bricks = [];
    score = 0;
    lives = 3;
    vx = 150;
    vy = -180;
    over = false;
    paddle = game.rect(W / 2, H - 20, 70, 10, 0x8fa8ff);
    ball = game.circle(W / 2, H - 60, 6, 0xffffff);
    for (let r = 0; r < 4; r++)
      for (let c = 0; c < 8; c++)
        bricks.push(game.rect(40 + c * 57, 40 + r * 20, 50, 14, [0xff4d6d, 0xffa64d, 0xffe14d, 0x7be069][r]));
    label = game.text('Score 0   Lives 3', { x: W / 2, y: 6, size: 18, align: 'center' });
  },
  update(dt, game) {
    if (over) return;
    paddle.x += game.keys.axis().x * 300 * dt;
    if (game.pointer.down) paddle.x = game.pointer.x;
    paddle.x = Math.max(35, Math.min(W - 35, paddle.x));
    ball.x += vx * dt;
    ball.y += vy * dt;
    if ((ball.x < 6 && vx < 0) || (ball.x > W - 6 && vx > 0)) {
      vx = -vx;
      game.sfx.play('bounce');
    }
    if (ball.y < 6 && vy < 0) {
      vy = -vy;
      game.sfx.play('bounce');
    }
    if (vy > 0 && game.overlaps(ball, paddle)) {
      // Where it lands on the paddle steers it.
      vy = -vy;
      vx = (ball.x - paddle.x) * 6;
      game.sfx.play('jump');
    }
    const hit = game.hits(ball, bricks);
    if (hit) {
      bricks = bricks.filter(brick => brick !== hit);
      game.burst(hit.x, hit.y, { color: 0xffe14d });
      game.remove(hit);
      vy = -vy;
      score += 10;
      game.sfx.play('coin');
      game.shake(4, 0.15);
      if (bricks.length === 0) end(game, 'You win!', 'win');
    }
    if (ball.y > H + 10) {
      lives--;
      game.flash(0xff2040);
      game.sfx.play('hurt');
      if (lives === 0) end(game, 'Game over', 'lose');
      else {
        ball.x = paddle.x;
        ball.y = H - 60;
        vx = 150;
        vy = -180;
      }
    }
    label.text = 'Score ' + score + '   Lives ' + lives;
  }
});

function end(game, words, sound) {
  over = true;
  game.sfx.play(sound);
  game.text(words, { x: W / 2, y: 120, size: 32, align: 'center' });
  game.button('Play again', { x: W / 2, y: 200 }, () => game.restart());
}
```

### Platformer: gravity, platforms, a level wider than the stage

```js
const { play } = Egret;

const W = 480,
  H = 270,
  LEVEL = 1200,
  GRAVITY = 900;
let hero, blocks, coins, goal, vy, onGround, got, label, won;

await play({
  width: W,
  height: H,
  background: 0x1b2440,
  setup(game) {
    blocks = [];
    coins = [];
    vy = 0;
    onGround = false;
    got = 0;
    won = false;
    // A rect is placed by its middle. The ground, a wall at each end, then four platforms with a coin over each.
    const block = (x, y, w, h) => blocks.push(game.rect(x, y, w, h, 0x4a6fa5));
    block(LEVEL / 2, 255, LEVEL, 30);
    block(-10, H / 2, 20, H);
    block(LEVEL + 10, H / 2, 20, H);
    [260, 420, 600, 760].forEach((x, i) => {
      const y = i % 2 ? 145 : 195;
      block(x, y, 90, 14);
      coins.push(game.circle(x, y - 25, 7, 0xffd23f));
    });
    coins.push(game.circle(1000, 215, 7, 0xffd23f));
    goal = game.rect(1150, 215, 16, 50, 0x7be069);
    hero = game.rect(60, 200, 18, 24, 0xff6b6b);
    // Text is in the ui layer: it stays put while the world scrolls.
    label = game.text('Coins 0/5', { x: 8, y: 6, size: 16 });
  },
  update(dt, game) {
    if (won) return;
    // Keys, or a finger: hold a side of the screen to run, tap the upper half to jump.
    let run = game.keys.axis().x;
    if (game.pointer.down) run = game.pointer.x < W / 2 ? -1 : 1;
    hero.x += run * 170 * dt;
    const jump = game.keys.pressed('space', 'up', 'w') || (game.pointer.pressed && game.pointer.y < H / 2);
    if (onGround && jump) {
      vy = -420;
      game.sfx.play('jump');
    }
    vy += GRAVITY * dt;
    hero.y += vy * dt;
    onGround = false;
    // Pushed up out of a block, it has landed; pushed down, it has hit its head.
    for (const block of blocks) {
      const push = game.pushOut(hero, block);
      if (!push) continue;
      hero.x += push.x;
      hero.y += push.y;
      if (push.y !== 0) vy = 0;
      if (push.y < 0) onGround = true;
    }
    const coin = game.hits(hero, coins);
    if (coin) {
      coins = coins.filter(other => other !== coin);
      game.burst(coin.x, coin.y, { color: 0xffd23f, count: 8 });
      game.remove(coin);
      label.text = 'Coins ' + ++got + '/5';
      game.sfx.play('coin');
    }
    if (game.overlaps(hero, goal)) {
      won = true;
      game.sfx.play('win');
      game.text('You made it!', { x: W / 2, y: 80, size: 28, align: 'center' });
      game.button('Play again', { x: W / 2, y: 150 }, () => game.restart());
    }
    // The camera follows the hero.
    game.view.x = Math.max(0, Math.min(LEVEL - W, hero.x - W / 2));
  }
});
```

### Memory: taps, turns that wait for one another, a best score

```js
const { play } = Egret;

const W = 360,
  H = 520,
  SIZE = 70,
  GAP = 12,
  BACK = 0x3a506b;
const FACES = [0xff6b6b, 0xffd23f, 0x7be069, 0x4dabf7, 0xb197fc, 0xff9f43, 0x63e6be, 0xf783ac];
let open, busy, pairs, moves, label;

await play({
  width: W,
  height: H,
  background: 0x14213d,
  setup(game) {
    open = [];
    busy = false;
    pairs = 0;
    moves = 0;
    label = game.text('Moves 0', { x: W / 2, y: 20, size: 22, align: 'center' });
    game.random.shuffle([...FACES, ...FACES]).forEach((face, i) => {
      const card = game.sprite(g => paint(g, BACK));
      card.x = 57 + (i % 4) * (SIZE + GAP);
      card.y = 115 + Math.floor(i / 4) * (SIZE + GAP);
      // A sprite takes properties of the game's own.
      card.face = face;
      card.up = false;
      game.onTap(card, () => flip(game, card));
    });
  }
});

function paint(g, color) {
  g.clear()
    .beginFill(color)
    .drawRoundRect(-SIZE / 2, -SIZE / 2, SIZE, SIZE, 16)
    .endFill();
}

// A card turns about its middle: narrow to nothing, change face, widen again.
async function turn(game, card, up) {
  await game.tween(card).to({ scaleX: 0 }, 0.1).done;
  paint(card.graphics, up ? card.face : BACK);
  card.up = up;
  await game.tween(card).to({ scaleX: 1 }, 0.1).done;
}

async function flip(game, card) {
  if (busy || card.up) return;
  busy = true;
  game.sfx.play('click');
  await turn(game, card, true);
  open.push(card);
  if (open.length === 2) {
    const [a, b] = open;
    open = [];
    label.text = 'Moves ' + ++moves;
    if (a.face === b.face) {
      game.sfx.play('coin');
      game.burst(a.x, a.y, { color: a.face });
      game.burst(b.x, b.y, { color: b.face });
      if (++pairs === FACES.length) win(game);
    } else {
      await game.wait(0.5);
      game.sfx.play('hit');
      await Promise.all([turn(game, a, false), turn(game, b, false)]);
    }
  }
  busy = false;
}

function win(game) {
  const best = Math.min(moves, game.load('best', moves));
  game.save('best', best);
  game.sfx.play('win');
  game.text('Done in ' + moves + ' moves\nBest ' + best, { x: W / 2, y: 425, size: 18, align: 'center' });
  game.button('Again', { x: W / 2, y: 492, height: 36 }, () => game.restart());
}
```

## 3D

`play3d` is `play` with a world of three dimensions under it. The page loads `egret3d.js` instead of `egret2d.js`, and the script starts with `const { play3d } = Egret;`. Everything above is the same and is the flat interface over the picture, in the units of `width` and `height`: `game.text`, `game.button`, `game.keys`, `game.pointer`, `game.sfx`, `game.tween`, `game.after`, `game.flash`, `game.restart`. What is added is the world. `x` is right, `y` is up, `z` is towards the camera; a ball of radius 0.5 on a ground of 24 reads well.

| Call | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `game.box(width, height, depth, color, { x, y, z })` | A box, its middle at the place |
| `game.sphere(radius, color, { x, y, z })`, `game.cylinder(radius, height, color, { x, y, z })`, `game.cone(radius, height, color, { x, y, z })` | A ball; a cylinder on its end; a cone on its base |
| `game.ground(size, color, y = 0)` | A square floor whose top is at height `y` |
| `game.add(model, { x, y, z })` | Makes a model of your own a thing: a `Mesh3D` of your geometry, a group, or a loaded glTF. Its box is worked out from its geometry; it keeps its colours |
| `game.remove(thing)` | Takes it out of the world; `thing.removed` is then true, and setting it does nothing |
| `game.onTap(thing, () => …)` | Calls the function when the thing is tapped or clicked: the nearest one under the pointer |
| `game.follow(thing, { x: 0, y: 4, z: 8, smooth: 6, turn })` | Keeps the camera that far from a thing, looking at it; `turn: true` keeps it behind as the thing's `rotationY` turns |
| `game.overlaps(a, b)`, `game.hits(a, list)`, `game.hitsAll(a, list)` | Overlap of things as upright boxes |
| `game.near(a, b, distance?)` | Whether their middles are within a distance, the sum of their radii unless given |
| `game.pushOut(a, b)` | How far to move `a` out of `b`: `{ x, y, z }`, one of them not 0, or `undefined`. A `y` above 0 means `a` stands on `b` |
| `game.shake(amount = 0.3, seconds = 0.25)` | Shakes the camera, in units of the world |
| `game.burst(x, y, z, { color, count, speed, life, size, gravity })` | Throws small pieces out from a point |

A thing has `x`, `y`, `z`, `rotationX`, `rotationY`, `rotationZ` (degrees), `scale`, `scaleX`, `scaleY`, `scaleZ`, `visible` and `color`, all of which can be set and tweened, and takes properties of your own. Without `follow`, set `game.camera.x`, `.y`, `.z` and call `game.camera.lookAt(x, y, z)`. `game.sun` lights the world and every thing casts and takes shadows: nothing to set. Shadows are drawn at the quality the device gets (`medium` or `high`); a software-rendered browser gets `low`, without them, and `game.app.setQuality('medium')` asks for them anyway. A turned thing is still tested as an upright box of its unturned size; `game.scene` and `game.app` are the World3D scene and app under it. There is no gravity: move things yourself, and use `pushOut` to stand them on one another.

`game.look('dusk')` sets the light and air of the world: `'day'` (as it starts), `'dusk'`, `'night'`, `'fog'` or `'snow'`, or `{ background, sky, ground, light, sun, sunIntensity, sunFrom, fog }` to change parts of one; `fog` is its thickness, 0 clear, 0.02 a haze, 0.06 a fog.

```js
const { play3d } = Egret;

const SPEED = 6,
  GRAVITY = 20;
let ball, blocks, stars, vy, got, label, done;

await play3d({
  width: 960,
  height: 540,
  background: 0x0b1020,
  setup(game) {
    blocks = [];
    stars = [];
    vy = 0;
    got = 0;
    done = false;
    // The ground is 24 across with its top at height 0; a box is placed by its middle.
    blocks.push(game.ground(24, 0x2d6a4f));
    blocks.push(game.box(4, 1, 4, 0x4d6fa8, { x: 6, y: 0.5, z: -4 }));
    ball = game.sphere(0.5, 0xe8453c, { y: 1 });
    for (const [x, y, z] of [
      [3, 0.9, 0],
      [-4, 0.9, -3],
      [6, 1.9, -4],
      [0, 0.9, 5]
    ])
      stars.push(game.cone(0.4, 0.8, 0xffd23f, { x, y, z }));
    game.follow(ball, { y: 6, z: 9 });
    // Text and buttons are the flat interface over the picture, in the units of width and height.
    label = game.text('Stars 0/4', { x: 16, y: 12, size: 28 });
  },
  update(dt, game) {
    if (done) return;
    // Keys, or a finger held on a side of the screen. On the ground x is right and z is towards the camera.
    const move = game.keys.axis();
    if (game.pointer.down) {
      move.x = game.pointer.x < 320 ? -1 : game.pointer.x > 640 ? 1 : 0;
      move.y = game.pointer.y < 180 ? -1 : game.pointer.y > 360 ? 1 : 0;
    }
    ball.x += move.x * SPEED * dt;
    ball.z += move.y * SPEED * dt;
    ball.rotationZ -= move.x * 300 * dt;
    ball.rotationX += move.y * 300 * dt;
    vy -= GRAVITY * dt;
    ball.y += vy * dt;
    // Pushed up out of a block, it stands on it.
    let onGround = false;
    for (const block of blocks) {
      const push = game.pushOut(ball, block);
      if (!push) continue;
      ball.x += push.x;
      ball.y += push.y;
      ball.z += push.z;
      if (push.y !== 0) vy = 0;
      if (push.y > 0) onGround = true;
    }
    if (onGround && (game.keys.pressed('space') || game.pointer.pressed)) {
      vy = 8;
      game.sfx.play('jump');
    }
    for (const star of stars) star.rotationY += 120 * dt;
    const star = game.hits(ball, stars);
    if (star) {
      stars = stars.filter(other => other !== star);
      game.burst(star.x, star.y, star.z, { color: 0xffd23f });
      game.remove(star);
      label.text = 'Stars ' + ++got + '/4';
      game.sfx.play('coin');
      game.shake(0.2, 0.2);
      if (got === 4) end(game, 'All four!', 'win');
    }
    if (ball.y < -12) end(game, 'Fell off', 'lose');
  }
});

function end(game, words, sound) {
  done = true;
  game.sfx.play(sound);
  game.text(words, { x: 480, y: 200, size: 48, align: 'center' });
  game.button('Play again', { x: 480, y: 300 }, () => game.restart());
}
```

## Check a game

In a checkout, `node tools/verify-game.mjs <absolute Playwright index.mjs> <game.html> <new output directory> [play.mjs]` runs the page in a headless browser, plays it blind with keys and clicks, and reports whether it started without an error, drew, kept running, changed under input and made a sound. Run it after writing or changing a game, and read the three pictures it saves.

Blind play does not reach a win or a loss. The optional `play.mjs` plays the game as a person would, in the stage's own units, and reads the page by the colour at a place:

```js
export const stage = { width: 480, height: 270 };
export default async function (player) {
  await player.hold('right');                                            // player.key('space') presses; player.tap(x, y) taps
  await player.until(look => player.alike(look(170, 150), 0x3b82f6), 'the button of the win screen', 30);
  await player.letGo('right');
  await player.picture('won');
}
```

## Beyond this page

`game.browser`, `game.engine` and `game.scope` are the engine under `play`; what the other entries make can be added to `game.world` and `game.ui`.

- [Play, in full](knowledge-base/en/docs/play.md): every option, sound recipes, what is checked
- [Graphics](knowledge-base/en/docs/graphics.md): gradients, dashes, arcs, image fills
- [The browser game](knowledge-base/en/docs/browser-game.md): images, labels and the loop without `play`
- [Audio](knowledge-base/en/docs/audio.md): music and sound files
- [The game kit](knowledge-base/en/docs/game-kit.md): input by action, gamepads, touch controls, larger saves
- [2D camera](knowledge-base/en/docs/camera-2d.md), [tile maps](knowledge-base/en/docs/tilemap.md), [particles](knowledge-base/en/docs/particles.md), [2D physics](knowledge-base/en/docs/physics-2d.md), [interface controls](knowledge-base/en/docs/ui-controls.md)
- [Play3D, in full](knowledge-base/en/docs/play3d.md), and [World3D](knowledge-base/en/docs/world3d-app.md) under it: models, materials, lights, physics
- [Error codes](knowledge-base/en/docs/error-codes.md) and [every entry](knowledge-base/en/docs/entry-points.md)

## Find more

For a larger game, ask the [guide](guide/index.txt) instead of reading more pages: it holds small cards, each learnt from games built on the engine. In a checkout, `node tools/egret-guide.mjs <words, an engine name, an error code or a devtools hint id>` prints the two or three cards that answer, and `--card <id>` prints one.
